prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the bright camera-wearer hand is nearest, roughly 0.2–0.5 m away, while the slats and work surface span the lower foreground at about 0.5–1.5 m; the standing woman is roughly 1–2 m ahead and the seated person is farther back, approximately 3–5 m away. The woman remains mostly left/front of the wearer before shifting toward the centre-right as the camera turns, and her extended hand closes from about 1 m to within arm’s reach and apparent contact in frame 5; the seated person stays behind her and to the right, several metres from both. Posts are resolved as vertical depth layers in front of the darker rear interior, making foreground/background separation and the increasing hand proximity clearer than in RGB alone. Absolute distances are only rough because the map supplies relative monocular depth, and it looks unreliable around thin slats, hands, silhouettes, and the dark background, where edges merge or depth detail disappears.
descriptions.segmentation: The map separates several people spatially: the standing woman occupies the left/front region in frames 1–4 and the centre-right in frame 5, while the seated person remains smaller and farther back on the right; additional tiny “person” masks in the background or near hands are mostly fragmented detections rather than reliable full bodies. The camera-wearer’s hand appears low in frames 1–3, then moves upward and rightward in frame 4, and overlaps the woman’s extended hand at arm’s reach in frame 5; their overlapping masks expose the final occlusion more clearly than RGB alone. A large foreground region is labelled “bench” in frame 3, roughly 0.5–1.5 m ahead and below the people, but most slats, posts, containers, and building surfaces are not segmented, so the overall scene layout and metric distance remain poorly specified. The map is unreliable where one person is split into multiple masks, hands are labelled as separate people, masks change colour or extent across frames, and thin or partly out-of-view objects vanish; facing direction and gaze cannot be established reliably from these silhouettes.
descriptions.pose: The pose map mainly isolates the camera-wearer’s magenta hand in the lower-left foreground of frame 1 and near the centre-right in frame 4, showing its change in position and articulated orientation more clearly than RGB; both detections correspond to a hand within roughly 0.2–0.5 m of the camera. In frame 5, a yellow body skeleton lies in the centre-right and a magenta hand skeleton overlaps its upper-right side, supporting that the standing woman is close, facing approximately toward the wearer, and that the two hands are within arm’s reach and partly occlude one another. The yellow body extends beyond the top edge, while scattered yellow keypoints near the bottom and top indicate partly out-of-view or uncertain joints; no dependable skeleton is shown for the seated background person, so their facing direction and reach cannot be inferred. Frames 2 and 3 contain no useful pose, and the frame-5 skeleton has implausible proportions and displaced keypoints, making exact body orientation, gaze, inter-person distance, and motion continuity unreliable.
